lede: Rebel space, held by the fleet that is already chasing you — the sector where the pursuit stops being background weather and becomes something your choices move. **Seven of the 49 events here touch the fleet clock, and six of them can only push it the wrong way**: a scout that lives long enough to charge its FTL doubles that jump's advance. The counterweight is not an event at all — reaching a nebula beacon halves the advance, so the sector's most dependable brake is whatever cloud the map happens to draw.
callout: **Two sectors hide in this one table, and they are mutually exclusive.** Roll high everywhere and the map fills before the last line is reached — the neutral pool goes, and with it {{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}}, the only event in the sector that can push the fleet **back**. Roll low and the table runs out before the beacons do, and the leftovers are drawn from a shared list that is not Rebel-flavoured at all — the one way a mercenary selling two jumps of delay ever appears here.

section_notes.HOSTILE_REBEL: Two of these five are scouts rather than warships. {{AUTO_WARNING}} and {{SQUAT_WARNING}} are ordinary fights right up until they start charging FTL — let either get away and that jump's advance doubles, which is the one thing killing them quickly actually buys. {{REBEL_TRANSPORT}} in the neutral pool looks identical and is not: its escape costs you nothing.
section_notes.BOARDERS_REBEL: Allocated one and exactly one, with no way to decline it. {{BOARDERS_SUN}} puts two to four humans aboard while you are sitting next to a star; {{BOARDERS_REBEL_SHIP}} sends two to three while a Rebel ship keeps firing.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_REBEL: Named after the shared fallback list, and not the same thing. Three of these eight — {{REBEL_TRANSPORT}}, {{BROKEN_REBEL_DRONE}} and {{AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}} — sit in that shared list as well, so they can still turn up on a map that never reaches this line; the other five, {{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}} and {{ALISON_DEFECTOR}} among them, are this line or nothing. Each of the three guarded Rebel installations has a way in that is not the fight: Sensors or a Teleporter at {{AUTO_DEFENSE_MAP}}, Cloaking at {{AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}}, a combat drone or Hacking at {{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}}.
section_notes.NEBULA_REBEL: Eleven events, and Sensors gets a branch in none of them; Cloaking appears in three and Engines in two. {{STORM_AUTO}} shows how the sector grades an escape — Engines 3 is a coin flip, Engines 6 and Cloaking are certainties — and {{NEBULA_AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}} does the same with Cloaking 1 against Cloaking 2.
section_notes.DISTRESS_BEACON_REBEL: Half of this list plants a marker somewhere else on the map: {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}} and {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}} both point at the hidden Federation base, {{ESCORT_BEACON}} hands you an escort job. The other half is where the risk is — {{TRAP_BEACON}} is a distress call that is really an ambush, and {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} is one of the four events here that can kill a crew member. Nothing outside this line carries the distress tag, which is unusual: in most sectors the marker leaks in from elsewhere, and here it never does.
section_notes.ITEMS: The one line in the table the Rebels do not touch — the same shared items list most sector definitions draw from, unchanged. Mostly a shop floor of stations, trades and sales, with {{FIND_WEAPON}}, {{FIND_DRONE}} and {{FREE_ITEMS}} the only outright gifts. {{HELP_MINERS}} is the only event in it that can produce an augment, and the branch that does it wants fifteen missiles.
section_notes.QUESTS_REBEL: Allocated zero to two, so a run can pass through offered neither — and even an offer can fail to land, because a marker needs a beacon that is unvisited, outside the clouds, not already taken by the fleet, and closer to you than the fleet is to it. Both events reach well past this sector: two of the five outcomes at {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}} advance the Federation-base thread, and the delivery job at {{MERCHANT_REQUEST}} ends at a research station whose survivors are infected — three to four boarders, and a crew member who turns on you.

steps.title: Three ways the marker gets planted
steps.detail: {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}} and {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}} in the distress pool, {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}} in the quest pool. On the loyalist transport it is the rescue branches that pay — the survivors are the ones who give you the coordinates.

steps.title: One roll at the marked beacon
steps.detail: Five outcomes: a drone from a barren planet, an outpost that gives you a crew member, a space-dock that repairs 35 hull and resupplies you, an apparently empty site, or the base already under attack.

steps.title: The empty site is not always empty
steps.detail: The dead-end outcome offers a second scan pass to **Sensors 2**, **Sensors 3** or **Long-Ranged Scanners**. The higher two turn nothing into a weapon.

steps.title: The base under attack
steps.detail: An auto-ship bombarding the outpost. Destroy it and a survivor joins you, with a weapon or a high standard reward on top. {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}} can plant this stage directly and skip the search entirely.

items.text: The default way out: past the storage-cache guard in clear space and in nebula, out of the plasma storm, and clean past the Rebel in {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}}. Only {{AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}} rolls for detection no matter what level you are carrying.

Boards the sensor station without provoking its guard, pulls the lost Federation crew out of the nebula, and is one of four ways to save the loyalists at {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}} — the one that gets you a crew member **and** the base coordinates.

{{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}} is the only brake on the pursuit in the whole pool: the Hacking branch delays the fleet a jump and reveals the map for one drone part, where the plain approach is a four-way roll that can trip an alarm and cost you a jump instead.
Pure escape, and graded — level 3 is a coin flip out of the plasma storm, level 6 is certain, level 4 loses the Rebel inside the cloud at {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}}.

The widest gate in the sector once the quest stages are counted — and dead weight at every nebula beacon, where the cloud shuts sensors off entirely. Level 3 reads the sensor station's map from a distance and scans {{BROKEN_REBEL_DRONE}} instead of waking it; level 2 and Long-Ranged Scanners both salvage the Federation base's dead end.

{{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} kills a crew member on anyone who walks in unaided. A Rockman walks through the fire for a high augment reward; a System Repair Drone does the same job for a drone schematic.
Twenty-three of the forty-nine events can hand you someone — by a distance the most common thing this sector gives, and mostly prisoners and survivors pulled out of ships you have just beaten.
{{REBEL_TRANSPORT}} is the richest single roll in the pool — eleven destroyed-outcomes covering military weaponry, a drone schematic, drone parts, a map reveal and a prisoner.
Only {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} behind Rock crew and {{HELP_MINERS}} for fifteen missiles produce one, and neither names it — both roll a random augment.

The hidden Federation base's space-dock outcome repairs 35, the largest patch anything in reach of this sector offers. Short of that it is {{REPAIR_STATION}} at 5, 10 or 20 for scrap and {{HELP_MINERS}} at 5 to 15 for missiles.
{{ALISON_DEFECTOR}} is the only event in the pool that names the species it gives you — a human, three times out of six, sometimes with a scrap cache attached.

{{AUTO_WARNING}}, {{SQUAT_WARNING}} and {{NEBULA_AUTO_WARNING}} if the scout escapes; {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}} if it spots you and lives; {{ALISON_DEFECTOR}} if the defector was lying; {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}} if you leave the civilians to die and they survive to report you.

One beacon of them is guaranteed, but six events can put people aboard: up to four humans at {{BOARDERS_SUN}}, {{NEBULA_REBEL_BOARDING}} and the infected station on {{MERCHANT_REQUEST}}, two to three at {{BOARDERS_REBEL_SHIP}} and {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}}, one or two at {{ALISON_DEFECTOR}}.

{{STORM_ITEMS}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}}, {{ALISON_DEFECTOR}} and {{MERCHANT_REQUEST}} are the only events that can take someone off the roster, and every one of them is a branch you opt into — nothing here costs crew on arrival.
{{AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR}} charges a drone part for the approach whether or not it works, including the outcome where the drone is shot down and the auto-ship comes for you anyway.
{{TRAP_BEACON}} is a distress call with a pirate behind it, and one of the five outcomes at {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}} is a Rebel signal broadcast specifically to catch ships like yours.

Reaching a nebula beacon halves that jump's advance, and how many the map has is settled before a single event is assigned. A cloud-free roll leaves the radar station as the only thing in the sector that can slow the fleet at all — and that sits in the line most likely to be cut.

A Rebel Elite Fighter under an anti-ship battery: three hull and a guaranteed breach per real shot, one fuel for the kill and no scrap, because the armada stops you stripping the wreck. Inside a cloud there is no battery — the beacon gains an ion storm instead, half your reactor and no breaches.

One or two are guaranteed and the line is filled early enough that the squeeze never reaches it. {{ESCORT_BEACON}} can open a third, and the shared fallback list carries a pirate briber who will sell you into one.

A planted marker still needs somewhere legal to land: an unvisited beacon, outside the clouds, not already taken by the fleet, and nearer to you than the fleet is to it. In the sector where the fleet is the whole problem, that filter is what quietly pushes quests into the next one.
